atoms.reference: An AI-based date-prediction model trained on 24 radiocarbon-dated scroll samples, applying Bayesian ridge regression to angular and allographic writing-style features; it predicted 14C-based dates with mean absolute errors of 27.9 to 30.7 years and, applied to 135 undated scrolls, aligned with 79% in palaeographic post-hoc evaluation. Its 14C ranges and predictions are often older than palaeographic estimates, giving a new chronology. It dates the copies, not the composition of the works; it offers probability-based options that aid palaeographers rather than replacing them; it is 'a first step', and 'more research is needed' on the relative typology.

evidence.record_quote: By applying Bayesian ridge regression on angular and allographic writing style feature vectors, Enoch could predict 14 C-based dates with varied mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 27.9 to 30.7 years.
the trained Enoch model then computed date predictions for 135 non-dated scrolls, aligning with 79% in palaeographic post-hoc evaluation.
The 14 C ranges and Enoch’s style-based predictions are often older than traditionally assumed palaeographic estimates, leading to a new chronology of the scrolls
This study in style-based date prediction using the Enoch approach is a first step.
More research is needed to solve this issue.
NOT a composition date: it dates the copies
